Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the infra looked promising. Before we schedule a technical deep-dive I need to understand how Redwood handles billing for Dedicated capacity. A few specific items from finance:

- Do you offer monthly subscription invoices for reserved GPU pools, or is annual prepay the only discounted path?
- What does a true-up look like if our usage spikes above the committed pool mid-quarter?
- Can we submit a PO and pay Net 30? Any minimum term we should be aware of?
- Suggested GPU pool sizing for a production workload with 12k qps of short chat completions (average 60 tokens/response). Any throughput guarantees?

If you can share an example invoice schedule or a quote template that would help speed internal review.

Best,

Hi Laura — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. High level answers up front, then I attached a concise proposal that lays out two paths: monthly-billed reserved capacity (no prepay) and annual prepay with a larger discount.

Summary:
- Monthly reserved pool: invoiced monthly, Net 30 on approved PO. Pricing is slightly higher than annual prepay (typical 8–12% delta) but you keep flexibility to scale down at renewal. True-ups: we do a quarterly reconciliation. If sustained usage exceeds committed capacity beyond the quarter threshold, there is a pro-rated true-up for additional capacity consumed that quarter.
- Annual prepay: single invoice at contract start (or split as 50/50), 18–22% discount depending on commit size. True-ups still apply but are handled at renewal with an end-of-year reconciliation and crediting model.
- PO/Net terms: PO accepted; standard Net 30 for enterprise. We can support invoice references for Horizon PO numbers.
- GPU pool sizing: based on the workload you described (12k qps, 60 tokens avg) my initial recommendation is a committed pool of 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs with burst autoscale to +30% (burst billed on usage). That should get you within our 95th-percentile latency SLO at typical batch sizes. See attached proposal for more detailed perf assumptions.

I've attached: redwood-dedicated-proposal-v3.pdf (proposal + invoice schedule) and an initial quote spreadsheet. Rishi is cc'd for pricing approval/any special discounts.

Would you prefer we draft an SOW + PO template now or wait until you decide on monthly vs annual? Happy to accommodate whichever speeds procurement for you.

Thanks,

Marissa / Rishi — quick technical notes to include in the proposal language. Numbers below assume MPT-style 7B model family (production-optimized) with standard batching heuristics. If Horizon runs heavier models or longer sequences we should re-run.

- Baseline throughput: ~1,600 - 1,900 tokens/sec per A100-equivalent GPU for short-chat (high batch efficiency). With avg 60 tokens/response this maps to ~26 - 31 responses/sec per GPU, ~1,600 - 1,900 qps per 8-GPU pool (aggregate) depending on batching and request size distribution.
- Burst autoscale: typically billed per-minute granularity; burst is charged at usage rate (same per-usage unit price) with no additional premium. We recommend a 20–30% burst headroom for production traffic to absorb short spikes without triggering a permanent true-up.
- True-up trigger guidance: we define sustained overage as usage > committed capacity for > 14 consecutive days in the reconciliation window. For Horizon's traffic pattern, recommend committing 25% safety buffer (so 10-GPU committed) to avoid frequent quarterly true-ups.
- Throughput guarantees: we can offer a latency-backed SLO with a committed pool and an SLA credit structure for missed SLOs; details are contract-level.

If you want I can draft the short paragraph to drop into the SOW describing true-up timing and how burst invoicing appears on the monthly invoice.

-Aditya

Hi Laura — following up with a concrete option set after internal review. Attached is an updated quote (redwood-quote-2025-07-18.xlsx) and a draft SOW. Highlights: 

Option A — Monthly reserved (recommended for flexibility):
- Commit: 8 GPUs (A100-equivalent) baseline, autoscale +30% (burst billed by usage).
- Monthly invoicing, Net 30 on PO. Quarterly reconciliation; sustained overage (>14 days) prorates and is billed at the monthly usage rate.
- Discount: standard monthly reserved pricing (no prepay discount).

Option B — Annual prepay (cost-optimized):
- Commit: 10 GPUs prepay for 12 months (recommended 25% buffer).
- Payment: single invoice at start (we can split 50/50 on request).
- Discount: 20% off list for the proposed commit. End-of-year reconciliation handles any true-ups with crediting toward next term.

Additional commercial notes:
- PO and Net 30 accepted. Please include Horizon PO# on invoices (we'll use your PO reference when creating invoices).
- We can support a monthly invoice schedule for the annual prepay (i.e., you prepay and we send monthly invoices for internal accounting) if that helps your AR process — we typically map that as a prepayment ledger entry.
- SLA & credits: available as add-on in the SOW.

Next steps: if Option B looks good we can prepare an SOW + DocuSign for signature; if Option A, I can issue the first-month invoice once PO is received. Which path is preferable for you and procurement?

Thanks — copying Rishi for final discount approval (I recommended 20% for the annual commit).

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
